disease_label_per_paper: Acute Q fever diagnosed by metagenomic next-generation sequencing, presenting with fever, pneumonia, thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, and hepatitis
presentation_summary: 34-year-old man presented after 5 days of recurrent high fever, then had persistent fever, fatigue, headache, poor appetite, pulmonary infection, and liver injury after admission.
He raised pigs as an occupation and reported insect bite exposure; he had taken cephalosporins and antipyretics before hospital admission without durable response.

Admission physical examination recorded temperature 36.5 C, pulse 78/min, respiration 20/min, blood pressure 100/80 mmHg, slightly yellow sclera with non-yellow skin, bilateral thick breath sounds, a few moist rales in both lower lungs, and no abdominal tenderness.

Treatment-before-directed labs included WBC 5.0 x10^9/L, neutrophils 3.9 x10^9/L, hemoglobin 149 g/L, platelets 71 x10^9/L, CRP 93.15 mg/L, PCT 2.13 ng/mL, ALT 167 U/L, AST 143 U/L, total bilirubin 28.9 umol/L, fibrinogen 4.53 g/L, and D-dimer 1.75 ug/mL.
Chest CT showed infectious lesions in both lungs and bilateral interstitial lesions.

quality_warnings: Coxiella mNGS is kept in confirmatory_findings, not ordinary observations.

The ordinary evidence keeps the presentation syndrome: high fever, headache/fatigue, animal exposure, thrombocytopenia, high CRP/PCT, hepatitis, coagulopathy, bilateral lung lesions, and routine culture negativity.
